{{Short description|Contravariant functor to Set}}
In [[category theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], a '''presheaf''' on a [[category (mathematics)|category]] <math>C</math> is a [[functor]] <math>F\colon C^\mathrm{op}\to\mathbf{Set}</math>. If <math>C</math> is the [[poset]] of [[open set]]s in a [[topological space]], interpreted as a category, then one recovers the usual notion of [[presheaf (mathematics)|presheaf]] on a topological space.

A [[morphism]] of presheaves is defined to be a [[natural transformation]] of functors.  This makes the collection of all presheaves on <math>C</math> into a category, and is an example of a [[functor category]]. It is often written as <math>\widehat{C} = \mathbf{Set}^{C^\mathrm{op}}</math> and it  is called the '''category of presheaves''' on <math>C</math>.  A functor into <math>\widehat{C}</math> is sometimes called a [[profunctor]].

A presheaf that is [[natural isomorphism|naturally isomorphic]] to the contravariant [[hom-functor]] Hom(–, ''A'') for some [[object (category theory)|object]] ''A'' of '''C''' is called a [[representable presheaf]].

Some authors refer to a functor <math>F\colon C^\mathrm{op}\to\mathbf{V}</math> as a '''<math>\mathbf{V}</math>-valued presheaf'''.<ref>{{nlab|id=co-Yoneda+lemma|title=co-Yoneda lemma}}</ref>

== Examples ==
* A [[simplicial set]] is a '''Set'''-valued presheaf on the [[simplex category]] <math>C=\Delta</math>.
* A [[directed multigraph]] is a presheaf on the category with two objects and two parallel morphisms between them i.e. <math>C = (E \overset{s}{\underset{t}{\longrightarrow}} V)</math>.
* An [[arrow category]] is a presheaf on the category with two objects and one morphism between them. i.e. <math>C = (E \overset{f}{\longrightarrow} V)</math>.
* A [[Group action#Right group action|right group action]] is a presheaf on the category created from a group <math>G</math>, i.e. a category with one object and invertible morphisms.

== Properties ==
* When <math>C</math> is a [[small category]], the functor category <math>\widehat{C}=\mathbf{Set}^{C^\mathrm{op}}</math> is [[cartesian closed]].
* The poset of [[subobject]]s of <math>P</math> form a [[Heyting algebra]], whenever <math>P</math> is an object of <math>\widehat{C}=\mathbf{Set}^{C^\mathrm{op}}</math> for small <math>C</math>.
* For any morphism <math>f:X\to Y</math> of <math>\widehat{C}</math>, the pullback functor of subobjects <math>f^*:\mathrm{Sub}_{\widehat{C}}(Y)\to\mathrm{Sub}_{\widehat{C}}(X)</math> has a [[right adjoint]], denoted <math>\forall_f</math>, and a left adjoint, <math>\exists_f</math>. These are the [[Universal quantifier#As adjoint|universal]] and existential quantifiers.
* A locally small category <math>C</math> embeds [[full and faithful functors|fully and faithfully]] into the category <math>\widehat{C}</math> of set-valued presheaves via the [[Yoneda embedding]] which to every object <math>A</math> of <math>C</math> associates the [[hom functor]] <math>C(-,A)</math>.
*The category <math>\widehat{C}</math> admits small [[limit (category theory)|limits]] and small [[colimit]]s.<ref>{{harvnb|Kashiwara|Schapira|2005|loc=Corollary 2.4.3.}}</ref> See [[limit and colimit of presheaves]] for further discussion.
* The [[Density theorem (category theory)|density theorem]] states that every presheaf is a colimit of representable presheaves; in fact, <math>\widehat{C}</math> is the [[colimit]] completion of <math>C</math> (see [[#Universal property]] below.)

== Universal property ==
The construction <math>C \mapsto \widehat{C} = \mathbf{Fct}(C^{\text{op}}, \mathbf{Set})</math> is called the '''colimit completion''' of ''C'' because of the following [[universal property]]:

{{math_theorem|name=Proposition<ref>{{harvnb|Kashiwara|Schapira|2005|loc=Proposition 2.7.1.}}</ref>|math_statement=Let ''C'', ''D'' be categories and assume ''D'' admits small colimits. Then each functor <math>\eta: C \to D</math> factorizes as
:<math>C \overset{y}\longrightarrow \widehat{C} \overset{\widetilde{\eta}}\longrightarrow D</math>
where ''y'' is the Yoneda embedding and <math>\widetilde{\eta}: \widehat{C} \to D</math> is a, unique up to isomorphism, colimit-preserving functor called the '''[[Yoneda lemma#Yoneda extension|Yoneda extension]]''' of <math>\eta</math>.}}

''Proof'': Given a presheaf ''F'', by the [[density theorem (category theory)|density theorem]], we can write <math>F =\varinjlim y U_i</math> where <math>U_i</math> are objects in ''C''. Then let <math>\widetilde{\eta} F = \varinjlim \eta U_i,</math> which exists by assumption. Since <math>\varinjlim -</math> is functorial, this determines the functor <math>\widetilde{\eta}: \widehat{C} \to D</math>. Succinctly, <math>\widetilde{\eta}</math> is the left [[Kan extension]] of <math>\eta</math> along ''y''; hence, the name "Yoneda extension". To see <math>\widetilde{\eta}</math> commutes with small colimits, we show <math>\widetilde{\eta}</math> is a left-adjoint (to some functor). Define <math>\mathcal{H}om(\eta, -): D \to \widehat{C}</math> to be the functor given by: for each object ''M'' in ''D'' and each object ''U'' in ''C'',
:<math>\mathcal{H}om(\eta, M)(U) = \operatorname{Hom}_D(\eta U, M).</math>
Then, for each object ''M'' in ''D'', since <math>\mathcal{H}om(\eta, M)(U_i) = \operatorname{Hom}(y U_i, \mathcal{H}om(\eta, M))</math> by the Yoneda lemma, we have:
:<math>\begin{align}
\operatorname{Hom}_D(\widetilde{\eta} F, M) &= \operatorname{Hom}_D(\varinjlim \eta U_i, M) = \varprojlim \operatorname{Hom}_D(\eta U_i, M) = \varprojlim \mathcal{H}om(\eta, M)(U_i) \\
&= \operatorname{Hom}_{\widehat{C}}(F, \mathcal{H}om(\eta, M)),
\end{align}</math>
which is to say <math>\widetilde{\eta}</math> is a left-adjoint to <math>\mathcal{H}om(\eta, -)</math>. <math>\square</math>

The proposition yields several corollaries. For example, the proposition implies that the construction <math>C \mapsto \widehat{C}</math> is functorial: i.e., each functor <math>C \to D</math> determines the functor <math>\widehat{C} \to \widehat{D}</math>.

== Variants ==
{{main|Presheaf on an ∞-category}}
A '''presheaf of spaces''' on an ∞-category ''C'' is a contravariant functor from ''C'' to the [[∞-category of spaces]] (for example, the nerve of the category of [[CW-complex]]es.)<ref>{{harvnb|Lurie|loc=Definition 1.2.16.1.}}</ref> It is an [[∞-category]] version of a presheaf of sets, as a "set" is replaced by a "space". The notion is used, among other things, in the ∞-category formulation of [[Yoneda's lemma]] that says: <math>C \to \widehat{C}</math> is [[full and faithful functors|fully faithful]] (here ''C'' can be just a [[simplicial set]].)<ref>{{harvnb|Lurie|loc=Proposition 5.1.3.1.}}</ref>

A '''copresheaf''' of a category ''C'' is a presheaf of ''C<sup>op</sup>''. In other words, it is a covariant functor from ''C'' to ''Set''.<ref>{{cite web |title=copresheaf |url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/copresheaf |website=nLab |access-date=4 September 2024}}</ref>
